With today's release of the macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version, it contains a short video clip that appears to demonstrate the Visual Intelligence feature of Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods. Here's the clip for everyone to watch.

Hidden demo clip of camera-equipped AirPods found inside macOS 26.7

MacRumors discovered a short video clip in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version, in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to remember the book he is looking at. Siri's voiceover says:

The camera itself is not visible in the clip. The earbuds look very similar to the current AirPods Pro, with the most obvious difference being that the stem appears slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris has also uploaded the same clip to X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch the camera-equipped AirPods with the internal codename B790 as early as this year. Earlier, MacRumors also found references to B790 in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, including code for an "image stream".

Interestingly, these AirPods are reportedly separate from another camera-equipped model that Bloomberg mentioned, which Apple has been developing under the internal codename B798 and is expected to launch in 2027.

Given that Apple decided to include this demo clip in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to be officially announced at next month's iPhone event.

What are your thoughts on this clip? Feel free to share them in the comments section.
